utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Haxhibeqiri. As I did yesterday, I remind you that the solemn declaration continues to apply today to that evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Haxhibeqiri, you have said quite a lot so far. You said that you were involved with human rights, so could you please tell us where the village of Jablanica is on the territory of the Djakovica municipality?

utterances.speaker: Fuat Haxhibeqiri [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Are you aware that 16 civilians were killed in that village?

utterances.speaker: Fuat Haxhibeqiri [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Do you know that all of those civilians were not Albanians?

utterances.speaker: Fuat Haxhibeqiri [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Do you know that there was a provisional detention camp there in the village of Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: Fuat Haxhibeqiri [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour, could we have a date regarding this event?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that there will be an answer for my next question.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Are you aware that Ramus Haradinaj, Idriz Balaj, and Lahi Brahimi were charged for those crimes before this Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: Fuat Haxhibeqiri [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I know that they were invited to come to the Tribunal but I do not know what they were charged with. You mentioned 16 civilians. In fact I've got a list of 40 civilians here killed by the Serbian forces and they are all Albanian in that village.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Mr. Haxhibeqiri, why are you so partial when we are talking about the Albanians; you don't seem to know anything.

utterances.speaker: Fuat Haxhibeqiri [Resumed]
utterances.text: Never the human rights council had any access to go and find out the details you're talking about and you're talking about the wartime. Are you?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Do you know where Radonjicko lake is?

utterances.speaker: Fuat Haxhibeqiri [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Do you know about the crimes at Radonjicko Jezero?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Again Your Honour it would be helpful to have some kind of time-frame for these matters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I don't think it necessarily helps your case if you're not more specific in these questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this is -- we are talking about the period of 1998 now, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I think you have to make it clear in your questions the period that you're relating them to so the witness is able to focus his mind on the period that you're interested in.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we are talking about generally known allegations that were frequently mentioned in the media both in Kosmet and in Serbia. Much media attention was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It's not your job to give evidence here. If you want to establish that that's what you're asking about, then you can only do that through either asking the witness or presenting the documents you want to rely on as indicators of general knowledge. But you can't simply give evidence to that effect before us, and remember we come to this fairly ignorant of the background circumstances until we hear about it in the evidence. It's also our duty to exclude from our minds anything we've heard from other cases, so you've got to build your own evidence in this case, bearing that in mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I understood, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Haxhibeqiri, did you understand that all the time we were talking about this period 1998-1999?

utterances.speaker: Fuat Haxhibeqiri [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You mentioned during your testimony on the 7th of August, the bombing of a column of Albanian refugees near Terzija bridge by NATO planes. Do you know how many people were killed? We are talking about the 14th of April 1999.

utterances.speaker: Fuat Haxhibeqiri [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: What were you doing then, Mr. Haxhibeqiri?

utterances.speaker: Fuat Haxhibeqiri [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, I did not have access to the grounds where the fighting was taking place because the village is some 15 kilometres from where I live and it was war.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: We are talking about Terzija Most, Terzijski bridge, and an incident that took place on the 14th of April 1999.

utterances.speaker: Fuat Haxhibeqiri [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what I'm answering about. The bridge of Terzi.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: How far is Terzijski bridge from your house?

utterances.speaker: Fuat Haxhibeqiri [Resumed]
utterances.text: Eight kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Haxhibeqiri, in your investigations you only dealt with Albanian victims; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Fuat Haxhibeqiri [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course, because we didn't have access and possibilities to identify victims of other ethnic groups.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No further questions, Your Honours, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Cepic. Mr. Aleksic?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Haxhibeqiri. I'm Aleksandar Aleksic, lawyer from Belgrade. I'm going to be asking you questions on behalf of the Defence of General Nebojsa Pavkovic. I'm going to be asking you a number of very short questions. I will try to be as specific as possible and I would like to ask you to provide the shortest possible answers, if possible with yes or no. When you provided your statement to the investigators of this Tribunal, you provided certain information about yourself, and yesterday you repeated some of this information relating to your profession. I apologise but we did not receive a corrected transcript so I do have the draft or the working version, and on page 68, lines 3 to 5 of yesterday's transcript, you said that you worked in a shop owned by the Agimi family, the Agimi organisation, and that after the war you continued to work for the same organisation but then you were actually paid. This is what was in the transcript. So could you please explain, if that means that you worked before that?

utterances.speaker: Fuat Haxhibeqiri [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Agimi firm is not private but state-owned. And after the war the shop was burned and I continued to work for the human rights council where I am being paid. Up until now, we were working as volunteers. Up until then we were working as volunteers.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you please tell me what you're doing now? Are you still just a human right activist or --

utterances.speaker: Fuat Haxhibeqiri [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Now I am a project manager in a non-governmental organisation which is the Forum for Democratic Initiative.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell us something about your qualifications, about your education? Which schools did you finish?

utterances.speaker: Fuat Haxhibeqiri [Resumed]
utterances.text: High school.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: And up until 1995 you worked in that shop as a merchant or a salesman, up until the war actually?

utterances.speaker: Fuat Haxhibeqiri [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Up until the night when the bombing started on the 24th of March when the shop was burned.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I'm going to move briefly to a different topic. In your statement, you said that since you were the chairman or the president of that non-governmental organisation, you talked to over 1.000 people. Yesterday in the transcript, during the testimony in chief conducted by my learned friend Mr. Hannis. On page 11, line 6 and 7 of the transcript you said you talked personally with 100 people and that after that you read or looked over the other statements; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Fuat Haxhibeqiri [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: Also yesterday, in response to a question by my learned friend Mr. Lukic - and this is page 68, lines 10 to 12 of the transcript - you stated that you continued your investigations after the war and that for a while you worked for the International Crisis Group; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Fuat Haxhibeqiri [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: And that they gave you certain forms. Did you personally fill in those forms?

utterances.speaker: Fuat Haxhibeqiri [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: Now I would like to ask you to respond to the following question. How many of these forms did you fill in, if you can tell us?

utterances.speaker: Fuat Haxhibeqiri [Resumed]
utterances.text: More than 100, more than 100. Yes, yes, more than a hundred.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: So if I understood you correctly, these 100 statements were not part of those forms or is that the same thing, if you can tell us?

utterances.speaker: Fuat Haxhibeqiri [Resumed]
utterances.text: The same thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did the people that you interviewed sign -- actually, ignore that. Your work, did it consist of just work for the International Crisis Group and then you submitted those forms later?

utterances.speaker: Fuat Haxhibeqiri [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But the ICG people were there present during all the interviews.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: Thank you, but that wasn't my question. I'm going to move to another topic now. During the examination-in-chief by my learned friend Mr. Hannis and then yesterday in response to questions of my colleague, Mr. Lukic, you mentioned the events of the 7th to 11th of May in Djakovica or actually the fighting between the KLA and what you call the Serbian forces.

utterances.speaker: Fuat Haxhibeqiri [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry but I must repeat this. You said that on that occasion, 106 people were killed, 300 were arrested, some of them were processed; of them, some of them were released and some of them were transferred to a different place. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Fuat Haxhibeqiri [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please show the witness his statement, Exhibit 5 P2235. This is the last page. I think this is the last page in all the versions.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I only have the first page in front of me, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Does the Witness have the last page? If so, then it's -- I don't need to see it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the passage before the last, and it's the incident you talked about of the 17th [as interpreted] to the 11th of May. It's an action.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: And my question is, is this the same event you described during your testimony over these last couple of days, the same incident that you talked about. Sorry, on which page in my document and the document that I have is that found, because it seems that we've got different documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Paragraph --.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'm sorry to interrupt, Your Honour, but my transcript doesn't seem to be going forward. I don't know if it is on your monitors or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: No, it's not at the moment, and --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'm stopped at page seven, line 13.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yeah. And we're struggling to get the document to the end of his statement as well. So far as the document is concerned, it is the second-last full paragraph; is that correct? Is that correct -- yeah. So we're not wanting the declaration at the end, which is now on the screen. We wish the second-last paragraph which start -- which starts with the words - hold on - which starts with the words, "from 7 till 11 May, 1999, in Asim Vokshi street." That's the paragraph. But just before --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: -- let's find out why the transcript is not advancing. Do you know the answer to that? No doubt it will catch up with us. Let's carry on with the questions. Carry on, Mr. -- well, too bad. We're carrying on and it will just need to be resolved at some later stage by just re-listening to the evidence from the recording, but we're not going to be delayed by these technical glitches. Let's carry on, Mr. Aleksic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I answer?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: The question was whether this was the same event or not. Yes, and when you were providing your statement, you didn't mention the KLA. Is that correct? When you gave the statement to the investigators of this tribunal.

utterances.speaker: Fuat Haxhibeqiri [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I mentioned it, and I said that the fighting was between the KLA and the Serbian forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: When you gave your statement on the 28th of August, 2001. You said that.

utterances.speaker: Fuat Haxhibeqiri [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have said and talked about the same event in many interviews but -- and said the same thing. And -- and this statement here is -- is not complete because there was also 87 corpses who were buried without any ceremonial by the troops, by the Serbian troops.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: I wasn't asking you that. I'm sorry. Don't give me an answer that had nothing to do with my questions. In the beginning I asked you if you could provide brief answers, yes or no, if possible. Could you please look at the next page where it says that the statement was read to you aloud in the Albanian and that it contains all that you have said; is that correct? It's on the next page.

utterances.speaker: Fuat Haxhibeqiri [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I've said that this statement lacks a lot of detail. I've said that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: Mr. Haxhibeqiri, that is not what I have just asked you.

utterances.speaker: Fuat Haxhibeqiri [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've given my answer on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Just before you sit down, your question was that the declaration said the statement contains all that the witness has said. Where does it say that?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, it's the affirmation by the witness, so it comes after the statement or at the back of the statement where he says the statement was read back to me in the Albanian language and contains all that I have said, to my best recollection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That's not what it says in English. You see, it says "and is true to the best of my knowledge and recollection." It doesn't say it contains all I have said. Does it? Does it say that in another language and has it been wrongly translated into English?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the interpreters or the translators probably have this filed in the B/C/S or the Serbian but each witness acknowledgement contains the same statement and that was my question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: But your question was posed on the basis that the words of the witness acknowledgement are, that the statement contains "all I have said." Now that's not what it says in English and I want to know if there is some confusion between the two languages.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Absolutely, Your Honour. Perhaps I wasn't precise enough. I said that in all the statements that we received from the other side, each document that has the witness acknowledgement, and this is a standard form, it's probably filed. It states, "This statement has been read over to me in the Albanian language and contains everything that I have said to the best of my knowledge and recollections. I have given this statement voluntarily and I'm aware that it maybe used," and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, can we have on the screen the witness acknowledgement? We do have it in Albanian, and -- you see that, Mr. -- could you read that witness acknowledgement please, just read it slowly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I've read it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: But read it out so that we -- just read it -- read it out aloud, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "This statement has been read over to me in Albanian language and is true to the best of my knowledge and recollection."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Just stop there. That's not the words, these are not the words you're using to me, Mr. Aleksic. There is a difference between saying my -- this is -- "this is what I've actually said" and "this is all that I've actually said." They have two quite distinct things, and the witness has constantly told you this statement does not contain everything he has said but he's also saying that it's true. Now I want to be clear that there is no misunderstanding about what's actually in the witness acknowledgement.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I absolutely agree with you but this is not my fault. Perhaps the witness can look at the last page of the statement in Serbian, in B/C/S, and then the witness and I think Mr. Haxhibeqiri understands and can read the Serbian. Then he can read it out in Serbian just to see if I have made a mistake. This is an official translation of the Tribunal, it's not our translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I understand that but -- but I was directed by you to the Albanian. I didn't choose to go to the Albanian. Now that you direct me to the Serbian version I will go to it. So let's have the Serbian declaration, if we can, on the screen. Now, Mr. Haxhibeqiri, can you read that, please, in the same way, just the first sentence of it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "This statement has been read over to me in the Albanian language and contains all that I have said according -- to the best of my knowledge and recollection. I have given this statement voluntarily."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That's all we need to hear from you. All right. I note the difference in the language used. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. O'Sullivan?

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: I'd like to follow up on this last series of questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Sir, the statement that you have in front of you is in the Albanian language, correct?

utterances.speaker: Fuat Haxhibeqiri [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Now, when you were interviewed on the 28th of August 2001, you were only asked to sign the English-language statement; in other words, the Albanian-language translation of the statement did not exist at the time, did it?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: I couldn't hear the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Could you repeat your answer, please?

utterances.speaker: Fuat Haxhibeqiri [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw the statement here.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Correct. And your Albanian language statement in front of you?

utterances.speaker: Fuat Haxhibeqiri [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw it in Albanian.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: But it did not exist on the 28th of August 2001, did it, when you were interviewed?

utterances.speaker: Fuat Haxhibeqiri [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: The only statement that you signed is the English-language statement P2235?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CHOWHAN
utterances.text: I would beg to interrupt; forgive me for that. You see, the witness here is under oath and the best thing is which statements he accepts. If he has signed a statement previously, all that makes no difference. If you can kindly consider, that will curtail time, a waste of time. Could you please ask him which one he accepts and that would end the controversy, if you so please.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I think Mr. O'Sullivan's point is a different one, though. I don't think it's a question of whether the statement is accurate or not in itself at the moment. He wants to find out what existed in documentary form at the time the witness actually made the acknowledgement, and in view of the differences in language that we've just heard about that could be important. So I don't think we ought to interrupt at this stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: I'm coming to my point, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: My point is this: That when you were interviewed by a representative of the Office of the Prosecutor, he spoke to you in English and there was an Albanian interpreter and you responded in Albanian and the interpreter recounted what you said to him in English, correct?

utterances.speaker: Fuat Haxhibeqiri [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: And then on the spot they produced a hard copy of this English-language statement, correct? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Fuat Haxhibeqiri [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: And then you and the other two people present, the investigator and the interpreter, signed each and every page, correct?

utterances.speaker: Fuat Haxhibeqiri [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Of course before you signed it, it was read back to you, the English document was read back to you in Albanian by the interpreter who was present, correct?

utterances.speaker: Fuat Haxhibeqiri [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: And indeed at the end of the English-language --

utterances.speaker: Fuat Haxhibeqiri [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I say fighting, I mean the belligerent sides. Probably the interpreter has missed that thing, and, of course, I was rather excited, tense, probably, and I could -- they don't notice that and now I see it. So it's not explicitly mentioned in my statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: That's not where we are going here, sir.

utterances.speaker: Fuat Haxhibeqiri [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think this is what you mean: You mean what -- it's not there, that the forces have entered Asim Vokshi street and with whom did they fight, so that that part of the other side should be mentioned there because this is what I'm recounting you, that fighting, and the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It will help us all if you just deal with the questions one by one. Let counsel approach this in the way he wishes to approach it. So listen to the question and answer each individual question that's posed to you. Mr. O'Sullivan?

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Let me focus you again on my question. So far we've said that this English-language statement was read back to you, to you in Albanian by the interpreter. At that point, you accepted the statement and everyone present, you, the interpreter, and the investigator, signed each page and you yourself signed the last page of this statement, correct? I'm sorry, we didn't hear your answer.

utterances.speaker: Fuat Haxhibeqiri [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I repeated it three times, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Now, at no point after it was read back to you did you complain to the investigator that your statement was incomplete, did you?

utterances.speaker: Fuat Haxhibeqiri [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have complained that the translation is very weak. I didn't like the translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Who did you tell that to? Did you tell the OTP investigator that when you were sitting with him on the 28th of August 2001?

utterances.speaker: Fuat Haxhibeqiri [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I said it to myself. I didn't like the Albanian, seems rather colourless.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: That translation in Albanian you were looking at did not exist on the 28th of August 2001. My question is: Did you complain to the people who were interviewing you, sir, that your statement was inaccurate, incomplete or otherwise unsatisfactory? That's my question.

utterances.speaker: Fuat Haxhibeqiri [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: I have no further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Fila?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Mr. President, let us first clarify a particular matter that has been coming up here throughout. Mr. Hannis, when he reads the Albanian statements -- I mean, the Court holds it against the Defence for the fact that we do not use the same nomenclature. I have to say that we never got the Albanian versions of any witness's statement with the relevant numbers because all the originals are actually in English, as Mr. O'Sullivan explained to you just now. All the rest are translations into Albanian, into Serbian. It is useful to know that, that the original statement is actually the English statement. That is the point of what I wish to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Mr. Haxhibeqiri, my name is Toma Fila?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Before you go further, I don't know whether this is a complaint or not that's being made by Mr. Fila but I'd like clarification, Mr. Hannis. The document which the witness generally has been referred to is in Albanian, as you made clear, and is even numbered for his purposes with numbers which are different from the numbers in the other versions. The indications are that the Defence have never been given that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, they've been given that document, but with -- not the paragraph numbers that I handwrote on to give to the witness so that he could follow along when I was referring to paragraphs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Fila has just said he has never had the Albanian document.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: No. I think he said he never had the Albanian document with paragraph numbers written on them.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] None of us know Albanian.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: No, no, no. The words are: "I have to say that we never got the Albanian versions of any witness's statement." And then a separate sentence with the relevant number. So is that -- it's confined to that, with the relevant number? That's all you're complaining about.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's what I meant; the numbers, I mean. Don't know the Albanian language. That's our problem. I just wanted to assist the Court. I didn't want to complain.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Mr. Haxhibeqiri, I'm Toma Fila, an attorney at law from Belgrade, and I defend Mr. Sainovic. Let us just clarify something very briefly. What we've been dealing with here was the question of medical care in Djakovica. If I'm not mistaken, your statements show that medical staff were both the Serbs and Albanians and patients were probably both Albanians and Serbs and others. Do you agree with me on that?

utterances.speaker: Fuat Haxhibeqiri [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: As far as I understood what you were saying, as far as I understood what you were saying, your only objection was why the directors of the hospitals were Serbs, not Albanians. That's on page 1 of your statement. Apart from that complaint, do you have any other complaints as regards medical care in the period up to 1998 except for why the directors were Serbs?

utterances.speaker: Fuat Haxhibeqiri [Resumed]
utterances.text: All the organisations from 1990 --

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: I'm talking about the hospital.

utterances.speaker: Fuat Haxhibeqiri [Resumed]
utterances.text: You were asking me whether there was an Albanian director before that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The question, Mr. Haxhibeqiri, is whether medical care for the population in general in Gjakova until 1998 was adequate.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Actually, are you only bothered by the fact that the directors were Serbs or did you have any general complaints regarding health care? That is the only thing that's not clear. All the rest is clear.

utterances.speaker: Fuat Haxhibeqiri [Resumed]
utterances.text: They have changed everything, all the powers were taken over by the Serbs because everything was being orchestrated.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Just talking about health care. I'm just asking about health care. Did people get normal medical treatment?

utterances.speaker: Fuat Haxhibeqiri [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not the competent person to explain to you the situation in the hospitals. I believe yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You've got as good an answer as you're going to get.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. Thank you, thank you. I'm grateful no more is needed.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Do you think that with the qualifications that you have this and in view of the job that you held do you think that you're in a position to assess which doctor is better suited for the position of director of a hospital? Are you really authorised to think about that? Do you have the competence for that?

utterances.speaker: Fuat Haxhibeqiri [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have simply expressed my views of the situation then, how roles have been changed, how Albanians were replaced by the Serbs. I was not the responsible person to speak about other matters. I only know that they were replaced with Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Let's move on to another subject. Well, do you know -- I mean, if you know then we can move on; if not, well, let's move on. Do you know that Mrs. Sadako Agata, the UN high commissioner for refugees, came to Djakovica in 1998? If you know about that then we can move on.

utterances.speaker: Fuat Haxhibeqiri [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. Frankly, I don't know that. Maybe she was but I don't know it. A long time has passed since then.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: We mentioned this local security. These were Albanians. You know what I'm talking about, right? Okay, you know. So is it correct that this local security so it's not the police, this local security existed in more than 30 villages in the municipality of Djakovica and there were over 100 members of this local security, Albanians, that is? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Fuat Haxhibeqiri [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mentioned 53. I don't work using their names, I mean we found a list in the MUP building and which I submitted to the Honourable Court, to Mr. Hannis. I don't know the exact figure.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Well, you don't have to know the exact figure. Do you know what happened to these people when the KLA came?

utterances.speaker: Fuat Haxhibeqiri [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Did you meet them alive and well? Did you see them alive and well or perhaps did you mean them, in that interview that --

utterances.speaker: Fuat Haxhibeqiri [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know either of them, they are from the villages. None of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: You don't know whether they are alive, perhaps?

utterances.speaker: Fuat Haxhibeqiri [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Now we are quickly going to deal with a few matters to clarify them. Let me continue along these lines. You said that you collected about 100 statements and that the rest were collected by six lawyers, if I understood you correctly, lawyers working for your organization. Or perhaps they are not from your organization, I'm not sure. So I'm talking about the 1.000 statements. Do you do we understand each other? Now, I'm interested in the following: You did not say in which period of time these statements were collected and that's very important for the record. In terms of time.

utterances.speaker: Fuat Haxhibeqiri [Resumed]
utterances.text: You didn't ask me about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: I am the one who is asking the questions now.

utterances.speaker: Fuat Haxhibeqiri [Resumed]
utterances.text: July or August of 1999, for five months in succession.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness be asked to wait for the translation into Albanian, please? Because there is overlapping.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Haxhibeqiri, there is an ongoing problem here of you answering sometimes a little too quickly for the interpreters. Could you just wait a moment or two at the end of each question to allow the interpreter to complete the translation before you answer it. Just wait for the complete translation into Albanian, that's the best way, and then answer when you hear that. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise for that. This is due to the fact that I know Serbian. That's why I tend to answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It's not your fault. It's just an administrative difficulty we have. If you can make sure you listen until the interpretation is finished. Mr. Fila?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NOSWORTHY
utterances.text: Might I just ask for confirmation and clarification in respect to the time period and the statements taken. Does it refer to the 1.000 in full or to the 100?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, he himself took 100 statements and the total is about 1.000.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NOSWORTHY
utterances.text: Therefore, please could --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The total number of interviews was about 1.000.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NOSWORTHY
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... mention that it took us in relation to the 1.000 or to the 100. That is what I wanted to discover.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Has it been answered?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NOSWORTHY
utterances.text: Not as yet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Haxhibeqiri, there were in total 1.000 statements. When you say that they were -- the statements were taken in a period of four or five months from July or August 1999, are you referring to all 1.000 statements?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I mean all of them. From July, August, 1999 until December, I think. November, maybe December. They lasted for five months. I know because we have been paying people.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Four, five, six. You mentioned that there were six lawyers. Is that what the record reflects?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The witness will have to start answering again, says the interpreter.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They were people who worked in the court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: My recollection of this is that you said ten people but it may be an inaccurate recollection. How many people assisted the --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There were ten people who conducted the interviews.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: But I think that you said that there were six lawyers.

utterances.speaker: Fuat Haxhibeqiri [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were some lawyers but not all of them were lawyers. There were two or three whom I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: They are from your organisation?

utterances.speaker: Fuat Haxhibeqiri [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, no. No, they applied for that job through the ICG and they were accepted but ICG had also its own people who would conduct interviews as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Now I'm a bit confused but we'll clarify this very quickly. So as for these 1.000 statements, they include the statements collected by you and your group and the statements collected by the International Crisis Group through, their own people, the lawyers and so on.

utterances.speaker: Fuat Haxhibeqiri [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I don't have the interviews conducted by the ICG people but only those who were done by my own staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: So the lawyers were not working for you, right?

utterances.speaker: Fuat Haxhibeqiri [Resumed]
utterances.text: They worked for the ICG, not for me.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: You know their names perhaps?

utterances.speaker: Fuat Haxhibeqiri [Resumed]
utterances.text: One of them was called Ahmet Ahmeti, if I'm not wrong. Maybe later on they will come to my mind. I know them personally because we worked in two groups, I with my team worked in the rural areas, they worked in the town and then we changed places. I came to the town, they went to the villages.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Then I really have to apologise to you for insisting this long?

utterances.speaker: Fuat Haxhibeqiri [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: It says here that you personally conduct the 1.000 interviews and that's why we are dealing with this at such length. All right. So these report you sent on to the International Crisis Group?

utterances.speaker: Fuat Haxhibeqiri [Resumed]
utterances.text: All of them personally. I'm repeating it for the umpteenth time. Each of us conducted about 100 interviews.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: I understand that, and they all ended up at the ICG, right?

utterances.speaker: Fuat Haxhibeqiri [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Before you proceed, Mr. Fila, if you have now completed that point, there is some clarification I would like. You took 100 interviews. I understand that. How many did you read?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All of them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: How many is that? Roughly.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Roughly 1.000.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And were they all taken by people that you had responsibility for rather than people who were separately engaged by the ICG?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The statements collected or the interviews conducted by the team composed of 10 persons, they are all filed in the office for -- or the Council for the Defence of Human Rights and Freedoms.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Were these ten people all part of the Council for the Defence of Human Rights and Freedoms?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. We were two teams of five or six persons each.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So when you talk about dividing your work between the villages and the town, you're talking about these two teams, one working in the village while the other is working in the town?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. We worked simultaneously, one day we worked in the city, the other day they worked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Sorry, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CHOWHAN
utterances.text: Sorry, excuse me, may I request you for a question? Rather a clarification. Now, the authenticity of these statements is something important. Were these taken down verbatim, all what the maker of the statement said, and who ensured -- who ensured that those words were the words of the author? And added to that, my request is that if you tell us, was there a certification to the effect that this is a verbatim statement of the maker, please? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. During the interview, always there were representatives from the ICG who wanted to make sure that the interview was conducted properly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CHOWHAN
utterances.text: Well, I would again beg the question: What do you mean, sir, properly? Because a statement can be verbatim or it could be inspired. So could you deal more on this, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. As I said, we had questionnaires with questions, so the interviewees had to respond to the questions contained in the form. As I said, the form was ready-made. They had to respond to the questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CHOWHAN
utterances.text: But excuse me, do you have a copy of that form for showing us the --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CHOWHAN
utterances.text: With your permission, sir, can we see it?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, my only concern is that in our dealings with ICG, with regard to statements that they've provided to us they have been provided under Rule 70. I have no problem with the Court seeing what the standard form and the questions are but it appears that this is one that's filled out by a particular individual and may contain information that under the agreement that he might have had with the interviewee should not be disclosed without consent, et cetera. That's the only point I wanted to raise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It's an important point because the question isn't directed to the format of the question. The question that's being directed by Judge Chowhan relates to the way the answers are recorded and that means understanding the answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I understand that. I think the witness could answer that question in terms of how he conducted interviews and how he recorded information received from the interviewees without having to necessarily look at one individual's form.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You don't have a redacted form that we can look at.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I don't. I may be able to find one, Your Honour, or create one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The one that's been handed up, Mr. Haxhibeqiri, is that completed in Albanian?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, none of us is likely to understand anything that's said in the form at the moment. So we can look at it, I think, as an indicator of the layout of the form.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: That's fine, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: But I understand the sensitivity about exploring the matter further. So can we see the form, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CHOWHAN
utterances.text: The learned counsel could read the question, one or two, just top give us a sample of what that was. It's very, very important.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: As it's in Albanian, I would have to have the witness read it but I take your point, Your Honour. I think that's a good suggestion.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I might be of help to you in this regard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CHOWHAN
utterances.text: Just one or two sort of questions which are being asked. That's it. You know this bar examination questionnaire of New York, it asks everything and sometime it's only a little bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: If the witness has another form in front of him, perhaps we could have him read what some of the standard questions are.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CHOWHAN
utterances.text: He could show this to us later on, if you like.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] By your leave, how many forms has he got with him? It might be useful for us to see one or more of them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Hold on. Please don't answer that question, Mr. Haxhibeqiri, please. It's been made clear, Mr. Fila, that this information has been provided under Rule 70. Now, whatever view you and I may have about Rule 70, it governs the situation here and I think it applies to the disclosure of any of this material. It may be that some investigation can be made into whether it needs to be applied rigidly but at the moment we are faced with a situation where Mr. Hannis tells us that this material has been provided on a confidential basis. Now your only reason for asking the question you want to ask is no doubt to follow up a disclosure question and that rather leads to a different -- leads us into difficult territory so just hold on for the moment until we explore this a little further and then I'll give you an opportunity to say what you have to say about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now, what we propose to do is follow up this matter in this way. I will return this document to the witness. The witness can then answer some questions about how he completed the document as suggested by Mr. Hannis when he conducted interviews and counsel can follow on after that if they wish. I can assure you that the Trial Chamber takes nothing at all from this document other than its layout and that that layout indicates some answers which could be narrative or may not be. I can't tell by looking at them, and others which may simply be -- some are one-word answers but they also are capable of being the words of the witness but we need to find that out by asking questions. Mr. O'Sullivan?

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: There is one matter I would like to raise and it relates to Rule 70. I think there is an a distinction to be made on who in fact is in possession of this material. If it's the Prosecution, Rule 740 applies. If it's this witness or his organisation, that they have these statements, Rule 70 does not apply to him or his organisation. And if he has them we would request that they be provided to us, the Defence, by the witness. We are not asking the Prosecution who apparently could not get permission from the organisation. I'm assuming Mr. Hannis had asked and they denied his request, but he can confirm that. My point is, Rule 70 doesn't apply to the witness if he's in possession of these statements.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yeah. My concern about that is that that's not the way the rule has been interpreted by the Tribunal. I mean, I'm very sympathetic personally to the proposition being made by Mr. O'Sullivan but, as you know, before a material is disclosed in a Rule 70 basis to the Defence, orders are made by the Tribunal governing that and Rule 70 is regarded as applying to the Defence in spite of the way in which it's worded. Now, if it applies to that extent, then there may well be an argument that it applies to the witness as well. I don't think I'm in favour of making a rapid decision on this, should you wish to take the matter any further. Let's see where we get to with the questions that are going to be asked and then if you want to raise the matter further, then you're free to do so. So Mr. Sabbah, give this back to the witness. Now, Mr. Haxhibeqiri, what we would like to know is, when you were conducting interviews, how was it that you went about dealing with the form? Could you just explain that to us, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Preliminary questions, the form of the interview. 1, 1, are you ready to testify to The Hague Tribunal? Yes or no? And here is -- there is an answer to that. Second question: Have you been interviewed by another international organisation here or elsewhere? Have you been interviewed by any other international organisation here or elsewhere? For example, when were you a refugee? Basic information. Name, surname, place of birth, nationality, permanent address, temporary address, name of the father, date of birth, month, year, gender, profession, date of interview, month, and the year of interview. Place of interview, municipality, and the name of the interviewer. Information related to crimes. Please be clear. Were you a victim or a witness to a crime? For example, a murder, torture, sexual abuse, kidnapping, destruction of property, looting, persecution, or a forceful displacement? Please describe in the blank page. If you need further space, please use an additional page. And we are talking about this additional blank page overleaf.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: In the case of the one in front of you, when you ask about an account of an event being reported, who writes the account on the form?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We do, the interviewers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: In this particular one in front of you, was it necessary to go on to a blank page?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. If there is more text, there is the blank page overleaf.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: But in this particular one, that blank page is blank still; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So what you have in that document is a very brief description of some event.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Here they've mentioned the kind of crimes, starting from kidnapping. The first point is the kind of crime committed. It's the date when the place -- the crime took place, the place where it took place, and the time. Describe the event, the form says: And I listen to what they are saying, what they have to say, and I describe the event as they say it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And is the event described there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now, there are other questions after that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. The second one is, is kind of crime, displacement. And then it's the date, the place, and the time of the crime. And they describe how it happened when they were displaced. The form says, please describe the authors of the crime. For example, the VJ, the police, the paramilitary or civilians. How were they dressed? What weapons, vehicles or other equipment they used? Then names, addresses, ages, and the family relations of the other victims to this crime. And then additional information is required further down. Point 3, kind of crimes, destruction of property. Again, date, place and time when the crime took place. Were you a victim or a witness to the crime? They had to just put in circle one of these answers, whether they were the victim or the witness. Describe what happened. At the end, please describe the authors of the crime. For example, the VJ, the police, the paramilitary or civilians. How were they dressed? What weapons, vehicles or other equipment they used? Names, addresses, ages, and family relations of other victims of this crime. And additional information. Under point 4, kinds of crimes, continues. If it's murder, murder. If it's looting, looting. If it's rape and so on. As always, date of -- date, place, and time of the crime.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Is everything else, then, the same as you've already described? Now --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes. At the end, describe the forceful displacement. Were you forced to leave the house, yes or no? Who forced you to leave the house? For example, the VJ, the police, the paramilitaries or civilians. Where did you go? Please note the names of the villages or towns through which you went. Can you give us details on who ordered the crime and who was the author? Was it the police, was it the military or the paramilitary forces during the time of your displacement? At the end, it's documentation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You've mentioned displacement already earlier as the second of the items and now you've mentioned it again as either the fourth or fifth. Is displacement mentioned more than once on that form?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. But in every description, we are asking about the kind of the crime carried out and this is part of the form.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I understand that but is displacement there more than once because of different dates or for some other reason?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, of course, because there, there were many displacements.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now, at the end, is the form signed by anyone?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. These forms were sent to the ICG offices, they were translated into English, they were photocopied.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Is the one which you have in front of you one which you yourself completed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. A member of my team.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: How do you come to be in possession of that document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I just brought it as a sample to show what kind of crime has happened to this particular person and he survived that event. 30 others, 37 other people were killed on that particular occasion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: How many of the forms do you have with you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And is that one of the thousand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The -- there is some doubt about your answer to the question. Was the document signed at all by anyone.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. Here there is no signature. But they were there present during the interview and there was a translator all the time interpreting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And the people from the ICG every now and then intervened to clarify.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CHOWHAN
utterances.text: I'm not satisfied, sir, and therefor I, with permission of my lord, I'm asking this. Even in the first form, before you sent it to the crisis group, the organisation you are mentioning, and you took down or somebody wrote these forms, these were not signed by the person who was being interviewed? Did he not at all sign? This must be clarified. Did no one sign?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Fila, please continue with your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. But Mr. Hannis will not keep his word.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: What was his word?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yesterday, you said that we should agree on the length of the cross-examination. We managed to reach an agreement but you have used our time. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I'm sure it's been greatly to your advantage, Mr. Fila.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Witness, I apologise. I just wanted to clarify a further point. When you received this form from the crisis group, was it in Albanian or was it in English and then translated into Albanian, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: Fuat Haxhibeqiri [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Albanian, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Do you know who composed it?

utterances.speaker: Fuat Haxhibeqiri [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Well, I may be asking you to speculate now but don't you think that the original might have been in English and then somebody translated into Albanian so you could use it? However, if you don't know --

utterances.speaker: Fuat Haxhibeqiri [Resumed]
utterances.text: I haven't seen anything. I consider that these are very peripheral questions, rather unimportant.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Mr. Haxhibeqiri, as far as I can see, there is no mention either of the KLA or of NATO in this form?

utterances.speaker: Fuat Haxhibeqiri [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's mentioned in the answers given to the questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: There is no question concerning the KLA or NATO. Very well. Let's move on. But there is a question as to whether they are willing to testify before The Hague Tribunal. I'll try to move on quite fast. Can it be put on the record that the witness replied that this was the first question?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters note they did not hear the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: My question was whether there was a question in the form as to whether they were willing to testify before The Hague Tribunal and the witness answered that that was the first question in the form.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes. That's noted in any event from his original answers when he described the form.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Mr. Haxhibeqiri, you said that you were the president of the council for the protection of human rights and so on. May I conclude that based on everything you have said over the past few days, you dealt exclusively with human rights violations where Albanian human rights were violated? You did not deal with human rights violations where the victims were Serbs, Roma or others?

utterances.speaker: Fuat Haxhibeqiri [Resumed]
utterances.text: We have recorded the cases as they came to us. Whoever came to our office to record their case we've done it, and if they haven't turned up, come to our office to do that, then we are not aware.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: But did you conduct investigations on the ground throughout the time you were in that organisation? Did you investigate any cases of human rights violations where the victims were non-Albanians, they were Turks, for example, or others?

utterances.speaker: Fuat Haxhibeqiri [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There were no Turks or others. I have gone -- I went to the offices of the Red Cross, International Red Cross, to check with them, and I've interviewed certain victims -- a certain number of victims there, and they are in the book, actually. And when I read the book, I heard about -- I heard about many other victims. I -- that's where I learned about the victims and how many people were missing, and they are in the book written by the International Red Cross and they are -- they appear there as missing or killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: I'm not asking about you personally.

utterances.speaker: Fuat Haxhibeqiri [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you that we haven't had access to those victims. They did not come to us to record their case. I don't know why they didn't come to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Yes. I understand that but my question was: Did you go to those places to see, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: Fuat Haxhibeqiri [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were not allowed by the police to approach them.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: After 1999, when you carried out these investigations, what police then prevented you from going? There, out on to the ground, to see there were no Serbs in Djakovica, for example?

utterances.speaker: Fuat Haxhibeqiri [Resumed]
utterances.text: No one prevented us then. We have evidenced all cases.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: That's my question, if you dealt with all human rights violations. Did you record any torchings of Serb churches, that those 3 per cent Serbs were no longer there, that you mentioned. As far as I know there are just a few women left. Did you notice that and, if you did, where did you write this down?

utterances.speaker: Fuat Haxhibeqiri [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were a few churches, in the centre of the city and there was one church there which was destroyed, after the war. It was a church which was built, there were political motives there.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: I just wanted to say very briefly the following: I visited your web site. On your site of your human rights centre, it always says that Albanian human rights were violated by Serbs. There were no other reports there. I'm only asking why, nothing more.

utterances.speaker: Fuat Haxhibeqiri [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've said that I have only recorded the cases for the people who have come to my office to our offices, and those who didn't come, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Are human rights a universal category or do they apply only to Albanians?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, that's argumentative.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It is argumentative and this question has been asked by a number of people and the answer has always been the same, we deal with the cases which are reported to us, and if you have an example of a Serb trying to report a case that has not been taken up by this organisation, then I would like to hear about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have one further question. It's evidently time for a break.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Do you know that before this Court, Mr. Abrahams and others testified, and that they observed human rights violations perpetrated by the KLA on the territory of Djakovica? Do you know anything about this? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: Fuat Haxhibeqiri [Resumed]
utterances.text: Don't know what he's testified but I have accompanied Mr. Abrahams on the ground during a visit there. What he has testified here, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: If you went there, didn't you see human right violations carried out by the KLA, if Abrahams saw those and he testified about that here? In Djakovica, there were human rights violations by the KLA, kidnappings murders, lootings, and so on. Are you trying to say that if Abrahams testified about this? He wasn't telling the truth?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour that's vague and compound, and I think there is no way the witness can answer that question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I agree, and I sustain the objection to that question. You'll need to reformulate it in a specific way that the witness can deal with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: If Mr. Abrahams said something like that, would you accept it?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Something like what, Your Honour? Like the previous vague question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yeah. What -- please put a specific question, Mr. Fila, to the witness. What is it you say Abrahams saw that you think this witness may also have seen?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Maybe it's time for a break, Your Honour, and then I will do that after the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CHOWHAN
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: We'll resume at five minutes past 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Fila?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To continue, Your Honours, where I left off, I would like the Chamber just to look at page 1038, lines 13 to 214 -- no, 13 to 24. This is testimony of Mr. Abrahams. I would like to just provide the Chamber with the basis for my question, why I put the question to this witness, Mr. Haxhibeqiri.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Mr. Haxhibeqiri --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Can we have this on the e-court or do we have to find it ourselves?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: We have to find the transcript ourselves. Which date are we talking about, Mr. Fila?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The 7th of August. Page 1038, lines 13 to 24.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, that relates to a specific period. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's 1998, Your Honour, you can see that at the top.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So if -- the first thing to establish is when the visit took place, that the witness accompanied Mr. Abrahams on.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's not what I wanted to ask. I just need a little time to finish.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Mr. Abrahams said in his testimony that in the subject period, 198 Serbs and Albanians disappeared, and that the KLA was responsible for that. Do you know anything about this? What is your comment on that?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm not sure that properly states what the transcript says, as far as the KLA being responsible for the 198 Serbs and Albanians disappearing. I think he indicated that was the number the Red Cross reported as disappearing but I'm not sure the link was stated. I don't have that transcript in front of me right at the moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: No, I think you're right, Mr. Hannis. The statement is: I'm not able to answer how many incidents were in particular but if I'm not mistaken I would have to consult with our reports but I think 198, both Albanians and Serbs went missing during 1998 and that figure is from the International Committee of the Red Cross. So the point Mr. Hannis is making, Mr. Fila, is that that could on one view be the total number of people who went missing no matter who was responsible for their disappearance. But the earlier part --

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I understand. Then I will ask him like this: Is he aware that in that period, in the territory of Djakovica, 198 people disappeared and that the KLA was responsible for all or some of those disappearances, ask him if he's aware of this or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Again, that's not completely accurate because there is not necessarily a connection with the KLA for any of the 198. It's possible. If the point my colleague wants to make is that Mr. Abrahams said he's aware of some human rights violations by the KLA in the Djakovica area in the spring and summer of 1998, I agree that's what he said.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I can assist, since this was the area that I was cross-examining Mr. Abrahams on. If you scroll up to my original question that elicited this response, you'll see I focused Mr. Abrahams exactly on KLA activities against the civilian population. So I believe that it is clear that he was testifying with respect to activities of the KLA against civilians. Looking at page 1038, line 3 through 12, which is the original question where I asked him to focus on KLA activities aimed at civilians in the Djakovica area and the response by Mr. Abrahams from 13 to 16 saying he doesn't know -- that most of the incidents he's familiar with are in this period and then we start talking about the incidents and he says, "I can identify how many incidents were in particular," and then he talks about the people missing based on what knowledge he does have. So I do believe that there is sufficient linkage in the transcript record that these incidents that we are talking about related to KLA activities against civilians.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I'll allow the witness to answer the question the way in which it was put. Mr. Haxhibeqiri, the question is are you aware that 198 people disappeared in the territory of Djakovica in the course of 1998? That's the first part of the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have records of about 160 cases of civilian victims in the territory of our municipality during that period.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And are you aware of --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mainly in the villages.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Are you aware of any of them being victims of KLA activity?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I'm not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Fila, you can take it on from there, if you wish.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Do you know if any of the victims were Serbs, any of the victims in the Djakovica territory? A victim of the KLA, I mean?

utterances.speaker: Fuat Haxhibeqiri [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: You were taking care about the protection of human rights in that area, right?

utterances.speaker: Fuat Haxhibeqiri [Resumed]
utterances.text: I read -- I read it in the book by the Red Cross and Natasa Kandic. It was there that I learned of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: And my last question: My last question is: On the first page of your statement, you mention a fact that I found no where else but there. I'm going to read that to you. You say that between 500 and 800 [as interpreted] Kosovo Albanian left Kosovo before 1998, so that was from the time that Milosevic came to power. How did you get this figure? We didn't find that anywhere else, not amongst the Red Cross figures or anywhere else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, I think the figure is wrongly recorded in the transcript. Hold on, please, Mr. Haxhibeqiri. Could you repeat the figure, please, Mr. Fila?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 500.000, not 50. 500.000 to 800.000, not 500 to 800.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 700.000.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Have you found that in your statement?

utterances.speaker: Fuat Haxhibeqiri [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. You said how have you come up with such figures? We saw reports published every day in our newspapers. You can identify the figures from the states that have taken in those Albanians. They must have the records of those immigrants. If -- you know, to have accurate figures, you can ask these states. Personally I have taken these figures from the newspapers. Even today a large number of them are abroad.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: First of all, which newspaper?

utterances.speaker: Fuat Haxhibeqiri [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ours.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: The newspaper you said that was not being published? All right, very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: 1999, I think.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I mentioned two newspapers that appeared then.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: All right. But until then it was. So how did you connect the 500.000 to 800.000, 500.000 to 800.000 -- no, actually to 700.000. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: So how did you connect that to Milosevic when Germany and others were talking about immigration but economic immigration. They went to work, there are some of my Macedonians there and my Serbs also.

utterances.speaker: Fuat Haxhibeqiri [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a political immigration. Yes, there have been people from other ethnicities that have left Serbia. This is a fact. But we were obliged to leave our country because of the violence exercised against us, because of the closing down of schools, of lack of employment, lack of prospective for the future. Mainly our youths had to leave the country.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: I didn't understand you.

utterances.speaker: Fuat Haxhibeqiri [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mainly youths were obliged to leave because of terror and violence.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Wasn't the youth from the whole of Yugoslavia at that time leaving, trying to find -- leaving, going abroad, because of the bad situation in the country? That is all.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm speaking about my own country.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Visnjic?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Haxhibeqiri, I am Tomislav Visnjic, and together with my colleagues, Norman Sepenuk and Marko Sladojevic, I am defending General Ojdanic. Mr. Haxhibeqiri, I will put some questions to you, also relating to figures, numbers. It will tie on to what my colleague, Mr. Fila, was saying. In your statement and in your testimony here before this Tribunal, you said that in the municipality of Djakovica before 1989, there was a total of 129.000 inhabitants; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Fuat Haxhibeqiri [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I said 120.000.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: 120.000, yes, I agree.

utterances.speaker: Fuat Haxhibeqiri [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since there is no census taken, figures can be manipulated. Recently they say the population is 150.000 -- 158.000, which shows that not -- no accurate figures exist because of lack of census. But I don't think that's important.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Haxhibeqiri, you also said that the percentage of non-Albanians never was higher than 2 per cent; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Fuat Haxhibeqiri [Resumed]
utterances.text: We are always talking about the last decade. I haven't heard of any other figure. It might be 2 or 3 per cent, roughly. I always refer to official figures.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: You referred to official figures so now I'm asking you: This estimate of 2 per cent and this estimate of 120.000 inhabitants, is that your own estimate or is that the figure of your organisation, the organisation that you were a president of for a certain period of time?

utterances.speaker: Fuat Haxhibeqiri [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said I refer to official statistics or figures. My organisation has never taken any population census. We've heard it, we've read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown Exhibit 3D6, page 3 of that document?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Haxhibeqiri, this is a document in the English language. I'm going to read two sentences to you from that document.
